# Syntakt: agent context pack

Data checked 2026-11-18, research snapshot `5a0b3743189d`. Generated from the Aggregat database; every item links back to the Markdown that is the source of truth. Everything here is second-hand: re-check addresses and byte patterns against the cited source before you rely on them. Evidence: `[hw]` seen on a real unit, `[emu]` emulator only, `[doc]` stated without a test result, `[?]` unclear or inferred.

Brief version: rules, recovery, bugs, incidents and open questions. The full pack [syntakt.md](syntakt.md) adds all facts.

## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc] [hw]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc] [hw]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [doc] [emu] [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [emu] [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]
- **A54** Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. [hw]
- **A55** Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu. [hw]
- **A56** On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module. [hw]
- **A57** On the Octatrack, do card I/O only where stock does its own (its card task), or load the data into RAM first; never read the card from the UI tick or a frame hook. [hw]
- **A58** A DSP test passes only when sound comes out, and check the analog outputs through a loopback, not only a USB recording. [hw]
- **A59** Check a firmware value against the audio output before you gate sound on it, and test in the mode the user plays. [hw]
- **A60** Every byte a mod stores in a stock record must pass stock's own check with the mod absent. [hw]
- **A61** Code hooked into the stock USB init must be safe in interrupt context and give the same result on every run (DT2/DN2). [doc]
- **A62** When you call a stock routine at a site other mods hook, set every register stock's own caller sets, not only the C arguments. [hw]
- **A63** When a USB interface's host-side setup can go stale on Windows, change `bcdDevice` with the release that needs it. [hw]
- **A64** When you hand the OS a structure, find out whether it copies it before use; later changes must go to the copy it reads. [hw]
- **A65** Judge a load budget by the playing load and include the new module's own cost. [hw]
- **A66** On a DSP that waits on a second core, put long work at the end of the frame, not at its head. [hw]
- **A67** Never raise a note's trig and its end in the same audio block. [hw]
- **A68** Before a software reset, anything the next boot must read has to be in RAM, not only in the cache. [hw]
- **A69** Take the stock bytes a run-time patch replays from a copy made before the OS and the flashed build ran, never from live RAM. [emu]
- **A70** Never land a change on the tick a stock event is due and rely on a tie between its time and the clock. [hw]
- **A71** Write at most one value per track, step and parameter in one change. [emu]
- **A72** When you extend a stock table that a setting indexes, extend every table that setting indexes, including tables the OS builds in RAM at run time. [hw]
- **A73** A neutral setting of an effect must give back stock's routing, not only a flat response. [hw]
- **A74** Build mod code with undefined-behaviour warnings as errors, at least `-Werror=return-type`. [emu]
- **A75** On the Model:Cycles, an added machine whose oscillator runs on through a trig must keep the stock VCA from cutting at the trig. [hw]
- **A76** Syntakt: never write SPI NOR `0x300000-0x380000`, and keep the OS container under 2 MB. [doc]
- **A77** Before you store mod data in a byte of a stock record, find every stock routine that reads or writes it, and test with a project that uses every feature of that record. [hw]
- **A78** When a base keeps its own data inside a stock record, shrink the core's area by the same bytes and refuse an overlap at build time. [hw]

## 2. Rules that name the Syntakt

- **C8** (C) Give every check a control that fails when the checker is broken. dnfw's LFO4 bridge passed every check and then faulted on a Digitone II. Three checks had reported success about work they never did: snapshot harnesses cleared code that no real boot had run; a boot gate printed "Safe to flash" after an unrelated edit had deleted its coverage section; and an emulator call returned 0 for a value that was present. Use a key nothing set that must read back absent, a routine list that must not be empty, a coverage line that must appear. A green result from an untested instrument is not evidence. `[hw]` {dn2-lfo4} Incidents: [I42](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i42-checks-reported-success-about-work-they-never-did). Test a safety mechanism's first step end to end through the production code: Synfact's safe-boot trial passed unit tests that replaced the eMMC write with a double, then crashed every boot on a Syntakt because the real table had no write function. Incidents: [I62](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i62-a-safe-boot-trial-crashed-every-boot), [I56](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i56-a-test-plan-pressed-the-wrong-key-and-the-emulator-reference-did-not-match-the-unit). For UI lifecycle tests, replay the actual edit and its notifications without manually repairing the next view. Armio's sampler tests explicitly reselected SYN before turning the sample knob; that hid a Machine-change path which left the old view attached. The corrected replay fails on R020 and passes the R021/R022 fix. `[emu]` {armio-r022} Incident: [I51](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i51-the-sample-popup-did-not-open-after-switching-machines). Run view opening and closing through the native push, compose, tick and cleanup, not through doubles: on the Syntakt a view a mod pushes is composed and ticked before the push returns, and stock's deferred cleanup can drop a close raised then, so Synfact's ARP pages stayed blank on the unit while stubbed tests passed. Publish a view's state before you push it. `[hw]` {synfact-1117} Incident: [I115](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i115-arp-pages-stayed-blank-or-lost-their-keys-after-permanent-mute-syntakt).
- **E5** (E) Test incremental working-state persistence separately from SAVE PROJECT. A mod's companion can pass explicit save/reload while remaining stale in the unsaved working backup. On DN2 1.11, native settings updates bypass the whole-project serializer; armio's sample extension missed that path. Exercise load, change and unload through real notifications, serialize the working backup, then restore into a fresh emulator without retaining its heap. Keep current-project ownership/UID checks and the same lock as pool mutations; do not replace a saved checkpoint or add storage work to the shutdown interrupt. A passing replay does not prove physical power-loss recovery or that a frozen task completed its queue. `[emu]` {armio-r022} Incidents: [I77](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i77-knob-assignments-a-mod-kept-in-a-kits-spare-bytes-were-lost-at-power-on) (Digitakt mk1: a cold boot after SAVE PROJECT drops kit spare bytes that LOAD PROJECT keeps), [I52](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i52-new-project-samples-were-missing-after-reboot), [I116](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i116-a-step-order-mod-missed-two-readers-of-its-state-syntakt) (Syntakt: a power cycle without a save restores kits from mirror slots that only `KitActive::kitChanged` re-encodes).

## 3. Recovery and flashing

- [doc] Syntakt (SyntHack OS `RECOVERY.md`): if the OS still boots, flash the stock `.syx` via Transfer's Drop page (works even if a mod misbehaved); if not, MIDI interface with a 5-pin OUT to the Syntakt's MIDI IN ("USB doesn't work from the startup menu"), FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, Transfer SYSEX TRANSFER "OS Upgrade via device startup menu", tens of minutes at 31.25 kbit/s, the unit restarts itself. Avoid TRIG 2 (empty reset) and TRIG 3 (factory reset) in the startup menu - both erase data. Do a dry run of the DIN procedure with the stock OS before the first flash; flash only files for which `tools/unpack/eft.py info <file>` reports `checksums : ok`; no hardware results are reported on the page. `[doc]` {synthack-recovery} (`recovery#2934ea2d`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:36](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L36))

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I20** Mod code at a "free" address crashed projects with certain samples. Cause: mod code at `0x46000000`, memory stock uses for those samples. Fix: v0.8.1 unpacks the mod code into a 64 KB block that a hook at the end of heap init (`0x4010358E`) reserves first. Rules: D11.
- **I50** Mod data written for default settings slowed project load and save. Cause: the ARP mod sealed a 320-byte carrier for every kit even with default settings, so load checked all 1,664 bindings; the project itself was valid. Fix: leave the carrier absent while all thirteen rows are defaults: 81 % fewer emulated instructions for a full serialization. Rules: E4.
- **I62** A safe-boot trial crashed every boot. Cause: the boot's eMMC accessor table had no write function, so marking the bank TRYING called address 0; the record never changed, so every boot retried the same bank. The unit tests had replaced exactly this piece with doubles. Fix: core 1.7.1 adds the write function, storage fails closed on a table without one, and an end-to-end test through the production loader reproduces the crash. Rules: C8.
- **I63** A mod's memory window broke the BASE/WDTH filter. Cause: the stock base-width filter reads Q31 poles from a 508-entry table with a zero tail and indexes up to 1023; Synfact's companion window sat in that tail, so BASE+WDTH of 128 or more read code as poles. Fix: core 1.7.2 bounds the index to 508. Rules: A43.
- **I64** A chorus running from DDR overloaded the Syntakt's MAIN CPU. Cause: all chorus code ran from DDR; about 5.4 KB of code was fetched per block. Fix: 0.2 moved the hot code and kernels into MAIN SRAM (0.2 KB fetched per block). Rules: A34.
- **I104** A development core put its module binder in boot storage that startup wipes. Cause: to free room in the resident reserve, the module binder had been moved into the storage appended after the MAIN image. Startup clears and reuses that storage once the resident copy is done, so the call from the machine loader jumped into wiped memory. The opcode audit and host tests passed because neither modelled the clearing, and the test fixtures filled the event lists directly instead of calling the binder. Fix: core 1.8.1.1 puts the binder and dispatcher back in resident memory; the builder now refuses startup entries that are not resident, and a new emulator test clears the appended storage and reproduces the exception at the same address as a negative control. 1.8.1.1 boots and plays on the unit. A failed bank may stay marked TRYING, so send it again and check the versions in System Info. Rules: A42,C8.
- **I115** ARP pages stayed blank or lost their keys after permanent mute (Syntakt). Cause: several, each hidden by a test double: the opening guard did not know MainScreen's six normal child views; a view pushed by the mod is composed and ticked synchronously before the push returns, so the mod's tick closed its own new view; and stock's deferred view cleanup (`0x40100ea4`) clears its pending flag after the visibility call, losing a close raised by a tick during that call, so a closed view stayed in the list and blocked ARP. Fix: ARP 1.10.4 selects its page before the push; core 1.8.2 clears the flag before the visibility call (same 18-byte window). Tests now run the native push, compose, tick and cleanup instead of stubs. Rules: C8.
- **I116** A step-order mod missed two readers of its state (Syntakt). Cause: the trig LEDs read the step through their own accessor `0x4008b734`, not the patched sequencer sites; and a power cycle without a save restores kits from their mirror slots, which are only re-encoded when `KitActive::kitChanged` (`0x40172250`) runs after a native kit edit. Fix: build 3 patches the accessor as a fifth site; build 10 calls `kitChanged` for the playing kit after each mode change (checked in Unicorn, not yet on the unit). Rules: E5,A31.
- **I139** A neutral filter setting still coloured the mix through the analog FX block (Syntakt Performance Mods). Cause: THRU left the whole mix routed through the analog FX block. Fix: TEST37c makes THRU a full bypass (filter off, stock routing kept, no CPU at THRU). Rules: A73.
- **I145** Many stock samples overwrote Synfact's resident core and crashed it at boot (Synfact). Cause: at boot stock concatenates all 64 stock samples into one blob in MAIN DDR from `0x4584f2c5`; past 84 s of audio in all it runs over the 64 KiB resident core at `0x46000000`. The core's guards checked each slot on disk and parsed the blob only after stock had built it. Reproduced in Unicorn for both OS versions (first overlapping write in stock's memcpy while copying slot 17). Fix: core 2.0.1 no longer calls the stock builder; it streams each sender page from eMMC with 5 KiB of scratch, and draws waveforms on demand. Rules: A34,D11.
- **I46** Syntakt startup-menu recovery tested over DIN. Cause: test. Fix: — Rules: A11,A36.

## 6. Open conflicts (sources disagree)

- **O1** Syntakt OS signing: A) SyntHack OS: 1.41 carries an HMAC-SHA256, with the key derived from the image B) digikit finding 70: 1.42 has no HMAC trailer; 2026-11-18 {digikit-st-1118}: no trailer slot at all (the container ends at section 8 rounded to 16; a stock rebuild matches byte for byte)
- **O3** Syntakt CPU #1 load: A) ~89 % of the audio interrupt at rest (SyntHack, measured with DTIM0) B) the render is 85.8k of 166.7k cycles per block (SY FM4)
- **O34** Syntakt OS container cap: A) Modwerk: at most 2 MB (the upgrade's receive buffer) {modwerk-st-goal} B) digikit `syntakt.toml`: `container_max = 0x300000`, copied from DT2/DN2 with the Syntakt flash map not read; digikit's own finding 141 puts the analog calibration record at NOR `0x300000` (backup `0x340000`), so a container from `0x80000` longer than `0x280000` would reach it {digikit-st-1118}
- **O35** Top of Syntakt DDR (OS 1.42): A) Modwerk freed `0x47fe0000-0x48000000` by lowering the stack 128 KB (one unit, with a sample reload) {modwerk-st-goal} B) digikit: `0x47c00000-0x48000000` is a 4 MiB ring cleared at boot and written every frame (static) {digikit-st-1118}
- **O36** Syntakt core clock: A) SyntHack: about 250 MHz (166,667 cycles per block) {synthack-docs} B) digikit assumes a 264 MHz core and 132 MHz bus (176,000 cycles per 1500 Hz frame) {digikit-st-1118}

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **H47** (stock) On Syntakt OS 1.42 the top 4 MiB of DDR (`0x47c00000-0x48000000`) is rewritten every frame while delay and reverb are in use, so Modwerk's freed `0x47fe0000-0x48000000` is not free then. Test: Fill `0x47fe0000-0x48000000` and `0x478c0000-0x47bf0000` with a pattern after boot, play a pattern with heavy delay and reverb sends, load a sample-heavy project, then read back. Settles O35.
- **H48** (stock) Holding TRIG 16 at power-on on a Syntakt with stock OS 1.42 does nothing else than (at most) toggle step 16 of the first pattern; MAIN has no boot-time key reader. Test: Hold TRIG 16 while powering on a stock unit; check the boot and step 16.
- **T4** (needs unit + SyntHack, effort M) Measure CPU #1 load with the digihealth DMA-timer method over the whole interrupt, at rest and busy
- **T5** (needs files, effort S) Check the trailer and HMAC of 1.40A/1.41/1.42 with your own files (elektron-firmware-tool, digikit)
- **T6** (needs files, effort M) Translate SyntHack/machine-45 anchors from 1.41 to 1.42 (byte patterns, not addresses) (tool: [`scripts/anchor_translate.py`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/scripts/anchor_translate.py), 2026-11-11: you supply both images; it reports per address whether the translation is exact, bracketed, one-sided or ambiguous)
- **T12** (needs files, effort M) Compare FPGA bitstreams across devices (sizes, SHA-256, header) and the OS code that talks to them. Leads: on the Rytm MKII, sample bit reduction is a command word sent to the external audio hardware, not PCM work on the ColdFire; and three bitstreams are exactly 54,664 bytes - Heat +FX section 1, A4 MKII section 1, and the Digitone mk1's (inside section 7, loaded by the second CPU)

Report results with the [test-result issue form](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/issues/new?template=test-result.yml).
